chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Miskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is in a state of taharah, then takes from his nails or his hair: should he repeat the wudu (ablution)?
He said: “No, but he should wipe his head and his nails with water.”
He said: I said: They claim that wudu (ablution) is required for it.
So he said: “If they dispute with you, then do not dispute with them; say: this is the sunnah (prophetic tradition).”

key_terms.أَظْفَارِهِ: his nails, in the context of trimming them
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), the normative practice being affirmed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before acts of worship
key_terms.شَعْرِهِ: his hair, in the context of cutting it
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: he wipes, meaning to pass water over lightly

ai.seo_question: Does cutting nails or hair invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that trimming the nails or hair does not require repeating wudu (ablution) for one who is already in a state of taharah. It instructs only wiping the head and nails with water, and it directs the believer to respond to disagreement by affirming that this is the sunnah (prophetic tradition).
